commit.message:
Chore: .gitignore untrack AI scratch files

The _CLAUDE folder holds single-use helper scripts and notes that are
local working material, not part of the project. Add it to .gitignore
alongside the other AI folders and drop the scripts that had been
committed by accident.

-"""Compare the working copies of the analytical references against their committed versions.
-
-Both files are read with h5py and every dataset is compared numerically, so a pure
-metadata or compression difference is reported as identical content.
-
-Run from the CADET-Verification root.
-"""
-
-import subprocess
-import tempfile
-from pathlib import Path
-
-import h5py
-import numpy as np
-
-FILES = [
-    'data/CADET-Verification_reference/analytical_frustumDispDPFR_1comp_benchmark1.h5',
-    'data/CADET-Verification_reference/analytical_radialDispDPFR_1comp_benchmark1.h5',
-    'data/CADET-Verification_reference/analytical_frustumAdvDPFR_1comp_benchmark1.h5',
-    'data/CADET-Verification_reference/analytical_radialAdvDPFR_1comp_benchmark1.h5',
-]
-
-
-def datasets(path):
-    out = {}
-    with h5py.File(path, 'r') as f:
-        def visit(name, obj):
-            if isinstance(obj, h5py.Dataset):
-                out[name] = np.array(obj)
-        f.visititems(visit)
-    return out
-
-
-for rel in FILES:
-    committed = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + rel],
-                               capture_output=True)
-    if committed.returncode != 0:
-        print(f"{Path(rel).name}: not in HEAD")
-        continue
-
-    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.h5', delete=False) as tmp:
-        tmp.write(committed.stdout)
-        tmp_path = tmp.name
-
-    a = datasets(tmp_path)
-    b = datasets(rel)
-
-    only_a = set(a) - set(b)
-    only_b = set(b) - set(a)
-    diffs = []
-    for key in sorted(set(a) & set(b)):
-        x, y = a[key], b[key]
-        if x.shape != y.shape or x.dtype.kind not in 'fiu':
-            continue
-        scale = max(np.max(np.abs(x)), 1e-300)
-        d = np.max(np.abs(x.astype(float) - y.astype(float))) / scale
-        if d > 0.0:
-            diffs.append((d, key))
-
-    if not diffs:
-        print(f"{Path(rel).name}: identical content")
-    else:
-        diffs.sort(reverse=True)
-        print(f"{Path(rel).name}: {len(diffs)} dataset(s) differ")
-        for d, key in diffs:
-            print(f"    {d:.3e}  {key}")
-    if only_a or only_b:
-        print(f"    datasets only in HEAD: {sorted(only_a)}")
-        print(f"    datasets only in working copy: {sorted(only_b)}")

issues.title: Fix consistent initialization of the 1D column model
issues.body:
This PR fixes:
1) consistent sensitivity  initialization of the 1D column model

The right hand side of the pure degrees of freedom was mapped from the start of the state vector instead of from the first pure degree of freedom, so it was shifted against the Jacobian block it is solved with by the number of components.

The quasi-stationary bound states read their subproblem Jacobian from a dense view that aliases the discretized system Jacobian, which neither owns a pivot array nor holds the undiscretized Jacobian the subproblem needs, and the known part of a shell was multiplied with a Jacobian block that spans the whole particle block rather than the shell.

The test helper only ever ran the first of its two binding modes, which hid all of this. Running both uncovers the same defects in the 2D column model, whose sensitivity initialization is marked as todo until they are fixed there as well.

2) AD consistent initialization of bound states

The quasi-stationary bound states of the 1D column model were initialized
from an uninitialized matrix when AD is used: the AD branch extracted the
cell Jacobian into the system Jacobian instead of the scratch matrix it reads back, and from directions that do not match the seeding.
Three further defects kept it from working: the scratch matrix for the nonlinear solver borrowed the sparse matrix index array as its LAPACK pivot, the seed vectors were lost because assigning a double to an active
clears its gradient, and an AD Jacobian adds entries to the system Jacobian, so its pattern no longer matched the discretized one.
The residual kernel only adds to the Jacobian, so the scratch matrix is cleared before it is filled, in the finite bath as well.

issues.title: Update CSTR interface to the particle type group interface
issues.body: Particle types are configured in particle_type_XXX groups now, as in the other unit operations, instead of the unit-level NBOUND, ADSORPTION_MODEL and INIT_CS fields. A unit operation selector can then pick between the CSTR and other 0D bulk models by particle transport type.

issues.title: Bump version to v6.0.0a5
Release v6.0.0a5
issues.body:
# CADET-Core Release Checklist

CADET-Core follows the semantic versioning system described at [semver.org](https://semver.org/), except for pre-release versioning, where we follow the PEP 440 style versioning, see e.g. [here](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/).

CADET-Core is released using the GitLab flow. In GitLab flow, feature and hotfix branches contain work for new features and bug fixes. These branches are merged back into the master branch immediately after they are finished, reviewed, and approved. The master branch is ready to be deployed but is not necessarily the source of truth for a new release. Each release has an associated release branch that is based on the master branch. Changes that are intended to be released are cherry-picked from master onto the release branch. The release is made on the release branch. Some release branches can be maintained, for example branch `v5.0.X` to support the last major release.

The following checklist describes the steps to execute sequentially for creating a new release.

---

## Preparation

- [x] Create a release branch `vX.X.X` (typically from `master`) and cherry-pick the commits to include
- [x] Create a version bump commit `Bump version to vX.X.X`:
  - Update the version number in `version.txt`, `zenodo.json` (two places), `cadet.hpp` and `cadet.doxyfile`
  - Update the authors list if needed in `AUTHORS.md` and `zenodo.json`
  - Update the file format in `driver.hpp` if required
  - Double check LATEST_CAPI_VERSION under `src\libcadet\VersionInfo.cpp.in`
  - Update `html_baseurl` and `smv_branch_whitelist` in the `doc/conf.py` file to the release branch (only if stable release)
  - If the release contains all commits from `master`, merge the bump commit into `master`

---

## Pre-release build and Docker image

- [x] Manually dispatch the `build_docker_containers` workflow ([cd_docker.yml](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/blob/master/.github/workflows/cd_docker.yml)) and input the commit hash of the last commit on the release branch.  
  This triggers the Docker workflow to build an image containing:
  - The CADET-Core version at this commit
  - The latest released version of CADET-Python
  - The latest released version of CADET-Process

---

## Continuous Deployment tests

- [x] Run the CD tests as described in the [CADET-Verification README](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Verification).
- [x] In the [CADET-Verification Output repository](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Verification-Output):
  - Open the automatically created branch for this release and compare the results with the previous release. To this end, there are comparison utility functions as described in the [CADET-Verification README](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Verification)
  - If the numerical engine or code structure changed, check the required simulation times
- [x] If tests fail or show unexpected behaviour:
  - Fix the issues on the release branch
  - Repeat the tests until results are as expected
  - Merge fixes into `master` and resolve conflicts if needed
- [x] Add the new run to the [meta-issue](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Verification-Output/issues/1) and upload the log generated from the convergence data comparison
- [x] Link the output branch in the release issue

---

## Creating the release on GitHub

- [x] Go to [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/releases/new):
  - Set the release branch as the target
  - Specify the tag `vX.X.X` according to semantic versioning
  - Add release notes with sections for Added, Fixed, Changed, and Updated
  - Double check: Publish pre-release or release, then publish.
- [x] Check creation of docker image with the new release
- [x] Verify Zenodo archiving:
  - Confirm that a version-specific DOI was created
  - Ensure that the source code and associated files are archived
  - Note that the [concept DOI](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8179015) remains constant

---

## Release of binaries on conda-forge

To ensure CADET-Core is accessible to a broad community, it is available as a Python package on conda-forge.  
Other software, such as CADET-Process and CADET-Python, import this package.
For pre-releases, make sure the `version` follows the conda-friendly PEP 404 standard in the following (e.g. 6.0.0a1). This version must also be the a tag of the release on GitHub (which it should already be at this point).

- [x] Go to your fork of [cadet-feedstock](https://github.com/conda-forge/cadet-feedstock) or create one if it does not exist
- [x] Create a new branch on your fork and change the file `recipe/meta.yaml`:
  - install openSSL
  - Generate the SHA256 key (replace `{{ version }}` with the semantic version number):  
    ```bash
    curl -sL https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/archive/refs/tags/v{{ version }}.tar.gz | openssl sha256
    ```
  - Update the version number and SHA256 key
  - Set the build number to zero (`build: number: 0`)
- [x] Open a PR onto the `main` branch (for a release) or the `dev` branch (pre-release) of `conda-forge/cadet-feedstock`, and complete the automatically generated checklist
  - Note: to check if the license file is included, check the tarball (`https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/archive/refs/tags/v{{ version }}.tar.gz`) if the License file is in the location specified in the meta.yml in the variable `license_file`
- [x] Wait for the automatic checks to pass
- [x] Merge the pull request to trigger the conda-forge release
- [x] Double check if the new version of cadet-core is on conda-forge

## Release of binaries on PyPi

Additionally, CADET-Core is released on PyPi.

- [x] Check if the workflow `wheels.yml` was successfully executed (triggered by the GitHub tag)
- [x] Check availability of the package on [pypi.org/project/CADET-Core/](https://pypi.org/project/CADET-Core/)

## Follow-up
- [x] Check if the documentation for the new version was deployed correctly: https://cadet.github.io/
- [x] Check whether a version bump of the [CADET metapackage](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Metapackage) is required. A bump is only necessary if the set of explicitly compatible CADET-Core and CADET-Process versions changes. This applies when a new CADET-Core release has feature parity with CADET-Process, or when a patch release is issued for a Core version that is already shipped as compatible in the metapackage.
- [x] Create or update a CADET forum post announcing the release, including release notes
- [x] If this release checklist was updated, add these changes to the corresponding issue template

issues.title: Fix cancellation in geometry-aware WENO smoothness indicators
issues.body:
I observed severe increase in IDAS timesteps for the radial-flow and frustum FV discretizations with very fine resolutions.
Increasing `WENO_EPS` solved it, and pointed me to the underlying issue:

reconstructRadial() and reconstructGeomExact() evaluated their smoothness indicators as the expanded quadratic form beta_r = sum_{m,n} B[r][m][n] u_m u_n.
Since beta vanishes for a constant stencil by construction, every B[r] annihilates the constant vector, so this evaluation order cancels |B| |u|^2 down to beta and leaves an absolute error of eps_mach |B| |u|^2 no matter how small the true beta is. At the salt scale of the SMA-LRMP benchmark (|u| ~ 371) that error is 1.3e-10 to 2.0e-10, and a flat stencil yields beta = -1.2e-10, so with the default WENO_EPS = 1e-10 the shifted indicator turns negative and alpha_r = D_r / beta_r^2 misses by a factor of about 39, differently for every cell and every residual evaluation. The results stay correct, but the residual becomes a noisy function of the state, which caps the IDAS step size. The effect is grid independent; the equidistant axial scheme is unaffected because it squares differences, as are the order 2 radial indicators, which are perfect squares already.

Evaluate the indicators in the factored form beta_r = sum_k (sum_m L[r][k][m] u_m)^2 instead. B[r] is symmetric positive semi-definite of rank at most order-1, so a symmetrically pivoted Cholesky yields L once the numerically zero mode is dropped. The factorization is verified against B and a rank beyond order-1 is rejected, which feeds the existing order-reduction fallback of prepareGeometryExactCoefficients(). Subtracting each row's mean enforces sum_m L[r][k][m] = 0, and accumulating the dot product over the differences u_m - u_0 makes beta exactly zero for a constant stencil, the invariant the expanded form violated. The analytic Jacobian uses d(beta_r)/d(u_m) = 2 sum_k L[r][k][m] (L[r][k] . u) at the same cost.

The geometry-exact coefficients are factored once per cell at setup, so the frustum pays nothing per call. The equidistant radial branch, however, derived its closed-form coefficients from zeta inside every reconstruction, which put the factorization into the residual evaluation and made reconstructRadial() three times as expensive per call. Precompute them per cell instead, in prepareRadialCoefficients(), mirroring prepareGeometryExactCoefficients() with the same order reduction and both flow directions; reconstructRadial() still evaluates them from its zeta argument when they have not been prepared. Same function and same zeta, so the stored coefficients, the reconstructed values and the Jacobians are bitwise identical to the on-the-fly ones. Since the whole coefficient evaluation now leaves the hot loop, order 3 costs 63-90 ns per call with the Jacobian against 99-111 ns before this commit.

SMA-LRMP at 128 cells, IDAS steps before -> after, with the outlet L_inf error against the DG P5Z256 reference of CADET-Verification unchanged in every case:

  axial      8235 ->  8235   (1.0182e-2)
  frustum   20680 ->  8608   (1.0679e-2)
  radial    26313 -> 10177   (1.1678e-2)

A frustum with both ends of the same radius, which runs the axial column through the geometry-exact reconstruction and must therefore reproduce the axial scheme, goes from 15606 to 8141 steps against the axial 8235.

issues.title: Add rapid liquid reaction to LRM DG
Fix transposed MCT exchange entries in Jacobian sparsity pattern
issues.body:
## Description of the PR

The MCT reserved the exchange entries in the Jacobian sparsity pattern as (origin, destination), but the exchange models write them at (destination, origin). Writes outside the pattern are dropped, so with one-directional exchange the coupling of the receiving channel to the origin channel was missing from the Jacobian. The solution was still fine, but forward sensitivities in the receiving channel were wrong (see #790 for details and an MRE).

This PR swaps the two arguments in `setSparsityPattern()`.

The 2-channel Jacobian tests already use one-directional exchange, and their FD pattern check was relaxed because it failed with `0.0 != -0.01`. That was this bug, so the tolerance is back to the default now.

Fixes #790

## Type of Change

🔹 **Bug fix**

issues.title: MCT sensitivities wrong for channels with one-directional exchange
issues.body:
This is a follow-up to #535. At the end of that thread we noticed that MCT sensitivities are wrong when a channel receives exchange but does not transport anything back (e.g. `e12 > 0`, `e21 = 0`), and that setting `e21 = 1e-20` works around it. #537 fixed the other part of that issue, but we never followed up on this one.

I think I found the cause. The exchange model writes the Jacobian entry at (row = destination, col = origin):

https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/blob/9e8a77a1/src/libcadet/model/exchange/LinearExchange.cpp#L236-L238

but the sparsity pattern reserves (row = origin, col = destination):

https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Core/blob/9e8a77a1/src/libcadet/model/parts/MultiChannelConvectionDispersionOperator.cpp#L1199

Writes to entries that are not in the pattern are silently dropped, so the entry only exists if there is also exchange in the opposite direction. The solution itself is still correct because Newton converges with the incomplete Jacobian, but the sensitivity system uses the Jacobian directly. This affects all parameter sensitivities in the receiving channel, not just exchange matrix entries. With no dispersion and no flow in that channel, the sensitivity is exactly zero.

Swapping the arguments fixes it:

```diff
-						pattern.add(idxCur_orig, idxCur_dest);
+						pattern.add(idxCur_dest, idxCur_orig);
```

I tested this with a 2-channel MCT (flow only in channel 0, `e01 = 0.01`, `e10 = 0`) and compared the `COL_LENGTH` sensitivity of channel 1 with central finite differences:

| | rel. L2 error in channel 1 |
|---|---|
| unpatched | 0.94 |
| unpatched, `e10 = 1e-20` | 3.3e-6 |
| patched, `e10 = 0` | 3.3e-6 |

It might be worth adding a case with one-directional exchange to the MCT sensitivity test from cadet/CADET-Verification#87, which currently uses two-way exchange.

<details>
<summary>MRE script</summary>

```python
"""MRE: MCT parameter sensitivities are wrong in a channel that only receives exchange."""
import numpy as np
from cadet import Cadet

Cadet.cadet_path = "/usr/local/bin/cadet-cli"  # adjust


def create_model(e01=0.01, e10=0.0, sens=True, filename="mre.h5"):
    m = Cadet()
    root = m.root
    root.input.model.nunits = 3

    root.input.model.unit_000.unit_type = "INLET"
    root.input.model.unit_000.ncomp = 1
    root.input.model.unit_000.inlet_type = "PIECEWISE_CUBIC_POLY"
    root.input.model.unit_000.sec_000.const_coeff = [1.0]
    root.input.model.unit_000.sec_001.const_coeff = [0.0]

    mct = root.input.model.unit_001
    mct.unit_type = "MULTI_CHANNEL_TRANSPORT"
    mct.ncomp = 1
    mct.nchannel = 2
    mct.col_length = 1.0
    mct.channel_cross_section_areas = [1.0, 1.0]
    mct.velocity = 1
    mct.col_dispersion = 1e-4
    mct.exchange_matrix = np.array([[[0.0], [e01]],
                                    [[e10], [0.0]]])
    mct.init_c = [0.0]
    mct.discretization.ncol = 100
    mct.discretization.use_analytic_jacobian = 1
    mct.discretization.reconstruction = "WENO"
    mct.discretization.weno.weno_order = 3
    mct.discretization.weno.boundary_model = 0
    mct.discretization.weno.weno_eps = 1e-10

    root.input.model.unit_002.unit_type = "OUTLET"
    root.input.model.unit_002.ncomp = 1

    # Only channel 0 receives flow; channel 1 is fed purely by exchange from channel 0
    q = 1e-2
    root.input.model.connections.nswitches = 1
    root.input.model.connections.connections_include_ports = 1
    root.input.model.connections.switch_000.section = 0
    root.input.model.connections.switch_000.connections = [
        0, 1, 0, 0, -1, -1, q,
        1, 2, 0, 0, -1, -1, q,
    ]

    root.input.solver.sections.nsec = 2
    root.input.solver.sections.section_times = [0.0, 20.0, 300.0]
    root.input.solver.sections.section_continuity = [0]
    root.input.solver.user_solution_times = np.linspace(0, 300, 301)
    root.input.solver.nthreads = 1
    root.input.solver.time_integrator.abstol = 1e-10
    root.input.solver.time_integrator.reltol = 1e-8
    root.input.solver.time_integrator.algtol = 1e-12
    root.input.solver.time_integrator.init_step_size = 1e-6
    root.input.solver.time_integrator.max_steps = 1000000
    root.input.model.solver.gs_type = 1
    root.input.model.solver.max_krylov = 0
    root.input.model.solver.max_restarts = 10
    root.input.model.solver.schur_safety = 1e-8

    root.input["return"].split_components_data = 0
    root.input["return"].split_ports_data = 0
    root.input["return"].unit_001.write_solution_bulk = 1
    root.input["return"].unit_001.write_sens_bulk = 1

    if sens:
        s = root.input.sensitivity
        s.nsens = 1
        s.sens_method = "ad1"
        p = s.param_000
        p.sens_name = "COL_LENGTH"
        p.sens_unit = 1
        p.sens_comp = -1
        p.sens_partype = -1
        p.sens_boundphase = -1
        p.sens_reaction = -1
        p.sens_section = -1
        p.sens_factor = 1.0
        p.sens_abstol = 1e-6

    m.filename = filename
    m.save()
    ret = m.run_simulation()
    assert ret.return_code == 0, ret.error_message
    return m


for e10 in [0.0, 1e-20]:
    m = create_model(e10=e10)
    ad = np.asarray(m.root.output.sensitivity.param_000.unit_001.sens_bulk)

    # central finite differences w.r.t. COL_LENGTH
    h = 1e-4
    mp = create_model(e10=e10, sens=False, filename="mre_p.h5")
    mp.root.input.model.unit_001.col_length = 1.0 + h
    mp.save(); mp.run_simulation(); mp.load_from_file()
    mm = create_model(e10=e10, sens=False, filename="mre_m.h5")
    mm.root.input.model.unit_001.col_length = 1.0 - h
    mm.save(); mm.run_simulation(); mm.load_from_file()
    fd = (np.asarray(mp.root.output.solution.unit_001.solution_bulk)
          - np.asarray(mm.root.output.solution.unit_001.solution_bulk)) / (2 * h)

    print(f"e10 = {e10:g}")
    for ch in range(2):
        err = np.linalg.norm(fd[:, :, ch] - ad[:, :, ch]) / np.linalg.norm(fd[:, :, ch])
        print(f"  channel {ch}: max|AD| = {np.abs(ad[:, :, ch]).max():.4g}, "
              f"max|FD| = {np.abs(fd[:, :, ch]).max():.4g}, rel. L2 error = {err:.2e}")
```

</details>

issues.title: Fix AD type mismatch in variable cross-section DG volume integral
issues.body:
`volumeIntegralMainImpl` in `ConvectionDispersionOperatorDG.hpp` multiplied a `double`-valued Jacobian matrix by the AD-typed state vector and cast the *result* to `ResidualType`, rather than casting the matrix first. That only compiles when the state type is `double`; it happened to also compile against Eigen 5.0.1's more permissive mixed-scalar-type resolution, but fails with a static assertion (`YOU_MIXED_DIFFERENT_NUMERIC_TYPES`) against Eigen 3.4.0, still the version most package managers ship. This matches the `if constexpr` cast-the-matrix-first pattern already used a few dozen lines above in `volumeIntegralAuxImpl` for the same reason. Verified the fix compiles cleanly against both Eigen 3.4.0 and 5.0.1.

Note: `volumeIntegralAuxImpl` additionally special-cases `ResidualType == double` inside its `StateType == double` branch to skip a same-type `.cast<double>()`. This fix doesn't add that extra split; it's not a perf regression since Eigen elides a no-op same-type cast, just a slightly coarser mirror of the existing pattern.

issues.title: Fix parameter dependent section slices in FV film diffusion for generalized units
issues.body:
For bulk FV discretizations, the model builder always checked for arrowhead optimization no matter which particle discretization was specified, disabling the combination of bulk FV and particle DG. This PR fixes the model builder accordingly.
Additionally, the FV film diffusion discretization used the raw film and pore diffusion coefficients instead of the appropriate parameter dependent section slice, which this PR also fixes.

issues.title: Add user-defined smoothly varying cross section geometry to the 1D column DG operator
issues.body:
The 1D column model so far offered three cross section area profiles: axial cylidner flow, radial cylinder annular flow, frustum.
This PR adds an arbitrary (smoothly varying) geometry to the 1D column bulk DG operator

The area must be given at every DG node, i.e. by exactly the degrees of freedom of
the nodal representation the operator uses everywhere else, and is represented
per element by the nodal Lagrange interpolant of those values. The area thus
lives in the same polynomial space as the solution.
The area weighted mass matrix M^A and the area and dispersion weighted matrix are integrated by Gauss quadrature that is exact for the resulting integrands, whose degree the interpolant raises by $N^d$. 
For a smooth area profile the interpolation error is of the same order as the discretization error of the scheme itself, so the representation does not reduce the order of convergence.

A new field `CROSS_SECTIONAL_AREA_AT_NODES` has (POLYDEG + 1) * NELEM entries, i.e. element interface nodes are listed twice.

EOC test Verification is conducted under [cadet-verification](https://github.com/cadet/CADET-Verification/tree/paper/column_geometries) with a cross-sectional area function changing under a sine wave

fixes #765

issues.title: Fix quadrature node count in variable cross section DG operators
issues.body:
The number of Gauss nodes for the dispersion- and area-weighted mass matrix was computed as

std::ceil((_axDispQuadDeg + geomFactorDegree + 2 * _polyDeg + 1) / 2)

Every operand is an integer, so the division truncated before std::ceil saw the result and the ceiling was a no-op. The expression therefore evaluated to floor((degree + 1) / 2) instead of ceil((degree + 1) / 2) and used one node too few whenever the integrand degree is even.

issues.title: Fix flow direction convention of radial and frustum geometries
issues.body:
The FV and DG discretizations disagreed on the orientation of the frustum: the DG operator places the large end at x = 0, whereas the FV operator built its cell radii from the small end, so the same input file produced mirrored state vectors. 
Both geometries now follow the convention that the interface documentation specifies: FORWARD_FLOW = 1 means flow from the larger towards the smaller radius, i.e. from the outer to the inner radius for the radial cylinder shell and from the large to the small end for the frustum.
